info.title: hearsay
info.description:
Local-first meeting-note transcriber. The core serves this API on `127.0.0.1` only, for the bundled web UI.

**Conventions**

- Base path is `/api`. Every request needs the session token; see the `session_token` scheme.
- List endpoints return `{ total, page, page_size, items }` and take `page` (at least 1, default 1) and `page_size` (1 to 200, default 50).
- Errors return `{ "detail": "..." }`. Database and internal failures render as a literal "internal error" — details go to the log only.
- Times are ISO 8601. Segment `start_s` and `end_s` are seconds relative to the meeting start, not wall clock.

**Not in this document**

Three served routes have no OpenAPI representation and are specified in `docs/api.md`: the live transcript WebSocket at `/ws/meetings/{id}`, meeting audio at `/api/meetings/{id}/audio` (a byte stream with `Range` support), and `/`, which serves the UI with the token injected.

get.description: Returned flat with each folder's `parent_id`; the client assembles the tree.

post.description: Omit `parent_id` (or send `null`) to create it at the root.

delete.description:
Cascade-deletes its sub-folders but un-files its meetings to the root. A folder operation never
deletes a meeting.

204.description: Deleted; its meetings were un-filed to the root

put.summary: Move a folder under a new parent.
put.description:
A `null` `parent_id` moves it to the root. A folder cannot become its own descendant; the cycle
is rejected rather than orphaning a subtree.

404.description: The folder or the target parent is unknown

422.description: The move would create a cycle

get.summary: List known people, most recently updated first.
get.description:
Every name that has ever been bound to a speaker, whether or not it has a stored voiceprint.
Powers the rename autocomplete, so a name used in one meeting is suggested in the next. For the
subset that can actually be recognized by voice, see `GET /api/voiceprints`.

patch.description:
Renames the identity and relabels every segment bound to it, across every meeting, in one
transaction, then re-exports each affected `transcript.md`. Generated notes are **not**
regenerated — they are model output rather than derived rows, so they keep the old name until
regenerated by hand.

A name collision is a conflict, never a silent identity merge. Re-applying the current name is a
no-op `200`.

409.description: Another person already holds that name

delete.description:
Clears every centroid stored for that person, including unlocked ones — otherwise an unlocked
sample would re-enter the candidate set as soon as its cluster was renamed. Names, locks, and
past transcripts are untouched; only future recognition stops.

204.description: All of that person's centroids cleared

get.description: Backs the Library and Dashboard views.

200.description: A page of meetings, newest first

post.description:
Spawns the capture helper, begins capture, and starts the transcription pipeline. One meeting
may be active at a time. `title` is optional; omitted, it defaults to a timestamp-derived name.

delete.summary: Delete a meeting and its recordings.
delete.description:
Removes the database rows (segments, clusters, and both notes tables cascade) and deletes the
on-disk folder. Irreversible. The active recording session cannot be deleted — stop it first.

patch.description:
Updates the title only; filing a meeting into a folder is a separate operation
(`PUT /api/meetings/{id}/folder`). The title is trimmed before it is stored.

put.summary: File a meeting into a folder.
put.description:
A `null` `folder_id` un-files the meeting back to the root. Organizational only — the meeting's
on-disk directory never moves.

404.description: The meeting or the target folder is unknown

post.summary:
"Keep recording": reset the active meeting's inactivity clock so a present-but-quiet user is not
nudged again or auto-ended. A no-op for any meeting that is not the current recording session
(404) — there is no clock to reset. Idempotent and cheap; the client calls it when the user
dismisses the "still recording?" prompt.

get.description:
Returns the Markdown `content`, the model that produced it, and timestamps, plus `edited` (set
once the notes have been hand-edited) and `stale` (`true` when the transcript changed after the
notes were generated, so the client can offer a regenerate).

404.description: This meeting has no notes yet

post.summary: Generate (or regenerate) meeting notes with the local LLM.
post.description:
Runs in the bundled `hearsay-notes` sidecar (llama.cpp, out-of-process) over the finalized
transcript. The model's reply is stored and returned verbatim as `content` — the user-editable
prompt template dictates the format, so nothing is parsed into structured fields.

Regenerating replaces existing notes, including hand-edited ones.

422.description: The meeting has no transcript to summarize

503.description: No notes model is configured, or the sidecar is unavailable

patch.description:
Replaces the stored Markdown `content` and sets the `edited` flag, which is what warns the user
before a regenerate overwrites their edits.

404.description: This meeting has no notes to edit

post.summary:
Pause the live meeting's capture (the "Pause" control): recording + transcription stop and the
timeline freezes with no gap until resumed. A 404 for any meeting that is not the current
recording session. Idempotent (pausing an already-paused meeting is a no-op 204).

post.description:
Re-diarizes and re-transcribes the whole Them track: global clustering, overlap handling, and
voiceprint recognition of people named in earlier meetings. More accurate than the streaming
labels, which run online with limited context.

Manual (locked) names are carried across. Segment-level work is not: per-line reassignments and
hand-edited text are rebuilt only at the cluster level, which is what the `edited` flag warns
about before the user starts a refine.

200.description: The meeting's speakers after the refine

503.description: The refine model or diarizer sidecar is unavailable

post.summary:
Resume a paused meeting's capture. A 404 for any meeting that is not the current recording
session. Idempotent (resuming a non-paused meeting is a no-op 204).

Open this meeting's recordings folder (audio, transcript, notes, meeting.json) in the OS file
manager — the per-meeting analog of the Settings "Reveal data folder" action, reusing the same
`open`-in-Finder helper. Runs in the core (a native process in the user's login session), reached
over the same-origin HTTP API. Failures surface the reason (not a generic 500) so a broken reveal
is diagnosable.

204.description: Handed off to the file manager

503.description: The folder could not be opened

get.summary: List a meeting's finalized transcript segments, ordered by `start_s`.
get.description:
How a past meeting reloads from the database, and how a live client recovers after a `resync`
event on the transcript WebSocket. Only finalized segments are stored; streamed partials are
never persisted.

200.description: A page of segments, ordered by start time

patch.description:
The database is the source of truth; `transcript.md` is re-exported best-effort afterwards.
Finalized meetings only — while recording, the live pipeline is still appending segments.

404.description: The segment is not in this meeting

422.description: Empty text, or over the length limit

patch.summary: Reassign one line to a different speaker.
patch.description:
Fixes an individual diarization mistake without renaming the whole cluster. Send exactly one of
`cluster_id` (move the line to an existing speaker in this meeting) or `display_name` (assign it
to a person by name, reusing that identity's cluster in the meeting if it has one, else creating
a new locked speaker).

The line is flagged `edited`, so it counts toward the warning shown before a refine discards
manual work. The database is the source of truth; `transcript.md` is re-exported best-effort.

404.description: The segment is not in this meeting

422.description: A Me line, an unknown target cluster, or a body that is not exactly one of the two fields

get.description:
Each item carries the cluster's resolved `label`: a bound name if the speaker has been named,
else `Speaker N`. Me is the microphone channel, not a cluster, so it never appears here.

200.description: A page of this meeting's speakers

put.summary: Name a speaker, binding the cluster to a cross-meeting identity.
put.description:
Gets or creates the identity by name, locks the binding, and relabels that speaker's segments.
A locked binding wins over voiceprint recognition and survives a re-diarize. If the meeting is
still active the name also propagates to the live pipeline, so subsequent utterances carry it.

404.description: The cluster is not in this meeting

post.summary: Combine two speakers the diarizer split apart.
post.description:
Folds the cluster named in the path into the one named by `into`: its lines are repointed,
relabelled to the target's name, and flagged `edited`, and the now-empty cluster is deleted.
Scoped to this meeting — no other meeting is touched, and the target's stored voiceprint is left
alone. The source's own voice sample goes with its row, so a spurious split stops feeding
recognition.

The freed ordinal is not reused, so labels can read "Speaker 1, Speaker 3"; renumbering would
rename unrelated speakers whose lines still carry the old text.

200.description: The meeting's speakers after the merge

404.description: The path cluster is not in this meeting

422.description: A self-merge, or an `into` cluster outside this meeting

post.description:
Stops capture, flushes the pipeline, rewrites `transcript.md` in timestamp order, and stamps
`ended_at`. Returns the updated meeting immediately: when a refine or notes step will run the
status is `refining`, and it flips to `finalized` once that background work completes.

get.summary: Read the user-authored "My notes" for a meeting.
get.description:
Free-form text the user types themselves, distinct from the LLM-generated notes. One row per
meeting. A `404` is the normal empty state — the panel starts blank.

200.description: The stored body and its last-saved time

404.description: Nothing has been typed for this meeting yet

put.summary: Autosave the user-authored "My notes" for a meeting.
put.description:
The database is the source of truth; `my-notes.md` in the meeting folder is mirrored
best-effort. Unlike the generated notes these may be written while the meeting is still
recording, so this route does not gate on the active session.

get.summary: The notes-model catalog, with each entry's installed state.
get.description:
A small fixed catalog of GGUF instruct models, plus the directory they install into. Always
compiled, independent of whether the notes sidecar is bundled, so the API surface is identical
across builds.

200.description: The catalog and the models directory

get.summary: The current model download's status, for polling.
get.description:
One of `idle`, `downloading` (with progress), `verifying` (checking the SHA-256), `ready`, or
`error`.

post.description:
Downloads into the models directory and verifies it by SHA-256 before marking it ready. One
download at a time; poll `GET /api/models/download` for progress.

get.summary: Full-text search across every meeting's transcript.
get.description:
Runs an FTS5 match over finalized transcript segments — not titles, and not notes. The query is
sanitized to plain terms (FTS operators are stripped) and bound as a parameter, so an empty or
all-punctuation query returns an empty page rather than an error.

Each hit carries the meeting, the matching segment, and a highlighted snippet, so a client can
jump straight to that moment in the transcript.

200.description: A page of matching transcript lines

get.summary: The effective settings: editable sections plus read-only build and storage facts.
get.description:
Returns every editable section (`recording`, `speakers`, `storage`, `models`) alongside the
read-only `storage_info`, `models_info`, and `about`. Each section's effective value is the
stored preference when one exists, else the environment default.

`models_info` reports the default refine and notes models, whether each file is present on disk,
and the default notes prompt, so the client can show what will run without the user having set
an override. `storage_info` adds `uncompressed_bytes` — how much is still held in un-archived
`audio.wav` files, which is what archiving would reclaim.

put.description:
Full-replaces the section: whether notes generation is enabled, which GGUF model runs it, and
the prompt template. The notes model path must exist and be a GGUF. The prompt's `{transcript}`
placeholder is filled at generation time.

422.description: A missing field, a model path that is absent or not a GGUF, or an over-long prompt

delete.summary: Reset the model settings to the environment defaults.
delete.description:
Clears the stored `models` overrides so the section falls back to what the environment
configures, and returns the resulting effective section.

200.description: The effective section after the reset

post.summary:
Open the bundled third-party notices in the OS default handler. Attribution for the CC BY 4.0
model weights has to reach the user from the distributed app, so the notices ship as a bundle
resource and Settings > About opens this copy. Routed through the core for the same reason as
[`reveal_output_dir`].

204.description: Handed off to the default handler

503.description: The notices file is missing or could not be opened

get.summary: Live OS permission status for the capture helper.
get.description:
Briefly spawns the capture helper and reads its permission snapshot and build version; nothing
is persisted. Degrades to `helper_available: false` with every field `unknown` when the helper
binary is absent, so a source build without the Swift side still renders the panel.

put.summary: Replace the recording and privacy settings.
put.description:
Full-replaces the section, so the body must carry every field — omitting one is a `422`, never a
silent reset. The inactivity prompt and the silence auto-end are gated independently: each
enabled threshold must be 1..=1440 minutes, and when both are on the auto-end must exceed the
prompt.

Takes effect from the next meeting; the effective settings are read at meeting start and stop,
so an edit never alters a meeting already in progress.

422.description: A missing field, or a threshold outside 1..=1440 / out of order

post.summary:
Open the effective recordings directory in the OS file manager. Runs in the core (a native
process in the user's login session), reached over the same-origin HTTP API the rest of Settings
uses — the desktop shell's Tauri `invoke()` is not reliably reachable from the webview's remote
loopback origin, so the "Reveal data folder" button routes here instead. On failure the reason is
surfaced to the client (not collapsed to a generic 500) so a broken reveal is diagnosable.

204.description: Handed off to the file manager

503.description: The directory could not be opened

put.description:
Full-replaces the section. `recognition_threshold` is the cosine similarity a stored voiceprint
must clear to auto-name a returning speaker: higher is stricter.

422.description: A missing field, or a recognition threshold outside 0.0..=1.0

put.description:
Full-replaces the section. `output_dir` must be absolute, existing, and writable. When
`compress_audio` is on, `compress_after_days` must be 1..=365 — a disabled threshold is inert,
and 0 is rejected because archiving the moment a meeting finalizes would race the post-stop
refine.

200.description: The stored section, with the output directory resolved

422.description: A missing field, an unusable output directory, or a compression threshold outside 1..=365

get.summary: The archival pass's current state, for polling.
get.description:
The same snapshot the POST returns: whether a pass is running, how many meetings it has to do,
how far it has got, and how many bytes it has reclaimed.

post.summary: Run the archival pass now instead of waiting for the periodic sweep.
post.description:
Returns immediately with the starting snapshot and does the work in the background -- a backlog
can take a minute of CPU, far longer than a request should hold. The UI polls the GET above.
Honors the effective age threshold, so pressing the button never archives a meeting the user's
own setting says is still too recent; it does not require the automatic sweep to be enabled,
since pressing it is an explicit instruction.

202.description: Accepted; the work list is already counted, so `total` is real and `running` is true

409.description: A meeting is recording, or a pass is already running

get.summary: Whether first-run model setup is still needed, and how a run is progressing.
get.description:
The installer ships no models. `required` stays `true` until the live and refine models are on
disk, and the UI blocks recording while it is. `steps` carries per-asset progress during a run,
and the work a run would do before one starts.

post.description:
Downloads the missing models in the background, plus the notes model named by `notes_model_id`.
Satisfied steps are skipped, so a retry after a failure resumes rather than starting over. Poll
`GET /api/setup` for progress.

get.summary: Live app readiness, for the UI header.
get.description:
Reports whether the transcription sidecars have finished loading their models. A cold start
takes several seconds, so the record control polls this to show a "preparing" state rather than
accepting a start that would stall. Read-only and cheap to poll.

get.summary: The voice roster: people who have a stored voiceprint, with all of their samples.
get.description:
Lists only people who **have** an embedding. Someone named in a meeting that was never refined
has no centroid and is therefore absent — they are still a known person on `GET /api/identities`,
just not a voice. Clearing someone's last sample drops them from this list, so `sample_count` is
always at least 1.

`active_count` is the subset recognition actually uses (a sample counts only once its name was
set by hand), so `active_count: 0` means "saved, matching nothing yet". `dimension` is the
embedding length — 256 on macOS, 192 on Windows — and samples of different lengths never match
each other.

200.description: A page of people with stored voiceprints

delete.description:
Clears that cluster's centroid and nothing else: the cluster, the name binding, and every past
transcript survive, and only future recognition changes. Idempotent.

AboutInfo.description: Read-only build facts for the About panel.

ArchiveState.description:
Progress of the audio-archival pass, whether started by the Settings button or the periodic
sweep. Polled by the UI while `running`; the counters describe the current pass, or the last one
once it has finished. Read-only.

CaptureHealthEvent.description:
A capture-health frame (not a transcript line): the named stream is delivering digital silence —
exactly-zero samples, which a working microphone never produces — so the UI warns that the mic is
muted or dead. Without this the failure is invisible, because ASR does not return nothing for
silence, it hallucinates text. Mirrors the orchestrator's `CaptureHealthEvent` on the wire.

state.description: Whether a capture stream is delivering audio (`ok`) or nothing at all (`silent`).

stream.description: The affected stream; only `me` (the mic) is monitored.

CaptureStateEvent.description:
A capture-state frame (not a transcript line): the meeting was paused or resumed (the "Pause"
control). Lets a live view freeze the timer/waveform on pause and resume them; also snapshotted on
WebSocket connect so a window reopened mid-pause reflects it. Mirrors the orchestrator's
`CaptureStateEvent` on the wire.

state.description: Whether live capture is paused or actively running.

CatalogEntry.description: One downloadable notes model in the in-app catalog (the internal repo/file/sha are not exposed).

installed.description: Whether this model's file already resolves in the models dir (downloaded).

DownloadRequest.description: Request body for starting a catalog download: the catalog `id` to fetch.

DownloadState.description: A snapshot of the (single, at-a-time) model download, polled by the UI like sidecar readiness.

message.description: A human-readable detail (an error reason, or the resolved path when ready).

model_id.description: The catalog id being downloaded (or last downloaded), if any.

DownloadStatus.description: Where a download is in its lifecycle.

FolderCreate.description:
Create a folder. `name` is validated non-empty, <= 255 chars; `parent_id` nests it under an
existing folder (omit or `null` for a root folder).

FolderRead.description:
An organizational folder for meetings (a node in the nested folder tree). `parent_id` is `null`
for a root folder.

FolderReparent.description:
Reparent a folder. `parent_id` is the new parent, or `null` to move it to the root. Validated: a
non-null `parent_id` must exist and must not be the folder itself or one of its descendants (which
would create a cycle).

FolderUpdate.description: Rename a folder. `name` replaces the folder's display name (validated non-empty, <= 255 chars).

IdentityRead.description: A known cross-meeting person (offered as a rename suggestion).

IdentityRename.description: Rename a person everywhere they appear.

LevelEvent.description:
An audio-level frame (not a transcript line): the recent RMS amplitude of a capture stream,
broadcast a few times a second so the UI can drive a live input waveform. Ephemeral — never
persisted or replayed to a new subscriber. Mirrors the orchestrator's `LevelEvent` on the wire.

rms.description: Root-mean-square amplitude of the recent audio, normalized f32 samples (`0.0..~1.0`).

stream.description: The stream this level is for (`me` or `them`).

MeetingCreate.description: Start a meeting. `title` defaults to a timestamp-derived name when omitted.

MeetingFolderAssign.description:
File a meeting under a folder. `folder_id` is the target folder, or `null` to un-file (move it
back to the root/"Unfiled" list). Validated: a non-null `folder_id` must reference an existing
folder.

MeetingNotesRead.description:
A meeting's generated notes for the API: the model's reply as verbatim Markdown `content`, and
which model produced them. The prompt template dictates the note's format, so there is no
structured summary/action-item shape.

edited.description:
Whether these notes have been manually edited (drives the "edited" badge + the regenerate
overwrite warning).

stale.description:
Whether the transcript changed after these notes were generated/edited — i.e. the notes may be
out of date. Computed at read time (a mutating response sets it `false`).

MeetingRead.description: A meeting row for the API.

folder.description:
The on-disk recordings-directory name (not an organizational folder). To move a meeting
between user folders, use `folder_id`.

folder_id.description: The organizational [`FolderRead`] this meeting is filed under, or `null` when unfiled.

MeetingStatus.description:
Lifecycle state of a meeting (lowercase on the wire): `recording` while live, `refining` while the
post-stop refine + transcript write run in the background, then `finalized`.

MeetingUpdate.description: Rename a meeting. `title` replaces the meeting's display title (validated non-empty, <= 255 chars).

ModelCatalog.description: The notes-model catalog + where downloads land, for the Settings > Models picker.

ModelSettings.description:
Models: the offline-refine whisper model path plus the optional local-LLM notes step (enable +
its GGUF model). Editable section; each effective value is the stored override, else the config
default. Live transcription is the FluidAudio/ANE sidecars and is not configured here.

notes_enabled.description:
Generate meeting notes at stop (the optional local-LLM notes step).
`#[serde(default)]` so a `models` row written before notes existed still deserializes.

notes_model.description: GGUF model path for the notes step; empty until one is downloaded or chosen.

notes_prompt.description:
User-editable prompt template for the notes step (its `{transcript}` placeholder is filled
with the finalized transcript). Empty means "use the built-in default"
(`ModelsInfo::default_notes_prompt`). `#[serde(default)]` so a `models` row written before the
prompt existed still deserializes.

ModelsInfo.description:
Read-only model facts shown alongside the editable models section: the bundled/config defaults
(reset targets) and whether each effective model file currently resolves on disk.

default_notes_prompt.description:
The built-in default notes prompt template (the reset target + the effective value when the
editable `notes_prompt` is empty).

NotesEdit.description: A manual notes edit: replace the Markdown `content`. Validated at the boundary (length-bounded).

Page_FolderRead.description: Paginated list envelope used by every list endpoint (`{ total, page, page_size, items }`).

items.description:
An organizational folder for meetings (a node in the nested folder tree). `parent_id` is `null`
for a root folder.

Page_IdentityRead.description: Paginated list envelope used by every list endpoint (`{ total, page, page_size, items }`).

items.description: A known cross-meeting person (offered as a rename suggestion).

Page_MeetingRead.description: Paginated list envelope used by every list endpoint (`{ total, page, page_size, items }`).

items.description: A meeting row for the API.

folder.description:
The on-disk recordings-directory name (not an organizational folder). To move a meeting
between user folders, use `folder_id`.

folder_id.description: The organizational [`FolderRead`] this meeting is filed under, or `null` when unfiled.

Page_SearchHit.description: Paginated list envelope used by every list endpoint (`{ total, page, page_size, items }`).

items.description:
One transcript-search hit for the API: the matched segment with enough meeting context to render
and navigate to it. `snippet` is the matched text with each match wrapped in the private-use
sentinels U+E000/U+E001, which the client swaps for highlight markup.

Page_SegmentRead.description: Paginated list envelope used by every list endpoint (`{ total, page, page_size, items }`).

items.description: A transcript segment for the API.

edited.description:
Whether this segment has been manually edited — its text or its speaker assignment (drives the
"edited" badge + the discard-on-refine warning).

Page_SpeakerRead.description: Paginated list envelope used by every list endpoint (`{ total, page, page_size, items }`).

items.description: A diarization cluster within a meeting, with its resolved display label.

Page_VoiceprintRead.description: Paginated list envelope used by every list endpoint (`{ total, page, page_size, items }`).

active_count.description: The subset that recognition actually uses (locked, with an embedding).

last_heard.description: Start of the most recent meeting a sample came from.

sample_count.description: Stored samples, whether or not they are recognition candidates.

PermissionsInfo.description:
Live TCC permission status probed from the capture helper (not a stored preference). Each field
is `granted` / `denied` / `undetermined`, or `unknown` when the helper is unavailable.
`helper_version` is the connected helper's build (`None` when unavailable).

PromptEvent.description:
An inactivity nudge (not a transcript line): the meeting has had no detected speech for
`silent_seconds`, so the UI shows a "still recording?" banner (Stop / Keep recording). If silence
continues to the end threshold the meeting auto-ends. Mirrors the orchestrator's `PromptEvent` on
the wire.

RecordingSettings.description:
Recording & privacy — the audio-retention switch (keep one WAV per meeting for playback + the
post-meeting refine) plus the inactivity watchdog: independently toggle the "still recording?"
prompt and the silence auto-end, with the silence thresholds in minutes (the prompt fires at
`inactivity_prompt_minutes`, the auto-end at `inactivity_end_minutes`, which must be the larger
when both are on). Editable section; a request body and part of [`SettingsRead`].

ResyncEvent.description:
A backfill signal (not a transcript line): the broadcast buffer dropped events for a lagged
subscriber, so the persisted transcript is ahead of this live stream. On receipt the client
refetches persisted segments rather than diverging.

SearchHit.description:
One transcript-search hit for the API: the matched segment with enough meeting context to render
and navigate to it. `snippet` is the matched text with each match wrapped in the private-use
sentinels U+E000/U+E001, which the client swaps for highlight markup.

SegmentEdit.description:
A manual transcript edit: replace a segment's `text`. Validated at the boundary (non-empty,
length-bounded).

SegmentRead.description: A transcript segment for the API.

edited.description:
Whether this segment has been manually edited — its text or its speaker assignment (drives the
"edited" badge + the discard-on-refine warning).

SegmentSpeakerAssign.description:
Reassign a single Them line to a different speaker. Provide exactly one of: `cluster_id` (an
existing cluster in the meeting) or `display_name` (a person by name — reuses that identity's
cluster in the meeting if it has one, else creates a new locked speaker).

SettingsRead.description:
The full editable settings, one field per panel/section. `storage_info` and `about` are
read-only context (not editable sections).

SetupRequest.description:
Request body for starting first-run setup: optionally a notes-model catalog `id` to fetch in the
same pass. The notes step is never required.

SetupState.description:
First-run model setup, polled by the UI. `required` is the gate: while it is `true` the app has
no models to record with, so the setup screen stays up.

message.description: A human-readable failure reason when `status` is `error`.

SetupStatus.description:
Where first-run model setup stands: `idle` (models missing, no run started), `running`, `ready`
(every model the app needs is on disk), or `error` (a run failed; retrying resumes it).

SetupStep.description:
One asset first-run setup fetches: the live speech models, the refine model, or a notes model.
`total_bytes` is approximate for the live models until the preparation sidecar reports its plan.

SpeakerMerge.description: Combine two of a meeting's speakers: the cluster in the path is folded into `into`.

into.description: The surviving cluster, in the same meeting.

SpeakerRead.description: A diarization cluster within a meeting, with its resolved display label.

SpeakerRename.description: Rename a cluster to a person (binds + locks; relabels that speaker's segments).

SpeakerSettings.description:
Speaker diarization: re-diarize each meeting at finalize (`auto_refine`) + the cosine at/above
which a refined speaker is auto-matched to a person named in a prior meeting.

StatusEvent.description:
A warm-up status frame (not a transcript line): a `warming` snapshot on connect for a cold start
and a `ready` transition once the sidecars finish, so the UI shows a "preparing" notice instead
of a silent gap.

kind.description:
The constant `kind` discriminant marking a [`StatusEvent`] (`"status"`), distinct from a
transcript line's `partial`/`final` so the client routes it off the transcript path.

state.description:
Whether the live transcription sidecars are still loading their models (`warming`) or have
finished and are serving (`ready`).

StatusInfo.description:
Live engine readiness for the UI to gate "Start" on. `sidecars_ready` is `true` once the
pre-warmed transcription sidecars have loaded their models (so a new meeting transcribes
immediately) and `false` while they are still loading after launch.

StorageInfo.description: Read-only storage facts shown alongside the editable storage section.

uncompressed_bytes.description: Bytes still held in uncompressed `audio.wav` files — what archiving would shrink ~3x.

StorageSettings.description:
Storage: the default root new meetings are written under (existing meetings keep their stamped
location), plus the audio-archival policy — once a finalized meeting is `compress_after_days`
old, its `audio.wav` is re-encoded as lossless FLAC (~3x smaller, bit-identical, so playback and
re-diarization are unaffected). Editable section; a request body and part of [`SettingsRead`].

compress_after_days.description: Days after a meeting ends before its audio is archived.

compress_audio.description:
Archive finalized meetings' audio as lossless FLAC. Deliberately NOT `#[serde(default)]`:
the PUT full-replaces the section, so a body omitting this would silently switch archival
off rather than leave it alone. Required means a partial write is a 422 instead.

Stream.description: Which capture channel a segment came from.

TranscriptEvent.description:
A live transcript line pushed to the meeting WebSocket: a `partial` (interim, speaker-less for
Them) or a `final` (persisted, with its resolved `speaker_label`).

kind.description:
The `kind` discriminant on a live [`TranscriptEvent`]: a pre-diarization `partial` (streamed, not
persisted) or a persisted `final`. Mirrors the orchestrator's `SegmentKind` on the wire.

UserNotesRead.description:
A meeting's user-authored "My notes" body (free-form text typed during the meeting). `body` is
empty when the user has typed none yet; `updated_at` drives the "autosaved" indicator.

UserNotesWrite.description:
An autosave of the user's "My notes" body. Length-bounded at the boundary (reject over-large
payloads as 422 rather than letting them reach the DB / the on-disk export).

active_count.description: The subset that recognition actually uses (locked, with an embedding).

last_heard.description: Start of the most recent meeting a sample came from.

sample_count.description: Stored samples, whether or not they are recognition candidates.

VoiceprintSampleRead.description: One stored voiceprint: the voice embedding kept on a single meeting's cluster.

dimension.description:
Embedding length: 256 on macOS (FluidAudio), 192 on Windows (sherpa). Samples of different
lengths never match each other.

id.description: The cluster carrying the embedding — a voiceprint has no id of its own.

locked.description:
Whether the name on this cluster was set by hand. Only locked samples are recognition
candidates in later meetings.

session_token.description: Per-process session token. `make rust-serve` prints it in the `open:` URL; the packaged app passes it to the webview through a handshake file. Channels that cannot set a header — the WebSocket and the audio element — take `?token=` instead.
